Book onto one of our school tours this term and come and see our wonderful school. Visit our Admissions page for dates and booking details. We look forward to welcoming you.
A WELCOME MESSAGE FROMThe Headteacher
Welcome to the Folly Hill Infant Academy website, we are an outstanding one form entry infant school in Farnham and part of The Kite Academy Trust. We are exceptionally proud to be a small, nurturing infant school where every child is known, valued, and encouraged to shine.
We believe that the early years of a child’s education are the most important, laying the foundation for a lifelong love of learning. Our dedicated and caring staff work closely together to create a safe, happy, and stimulating environment where children feel confident to explore, question, and grow.
Thank you for taking the time to visit our website. Please do get in touch if you would like to know more or arrange a visit—we would love to show you what makes our fantastic school such a special place to learn and grow.
Upcoming EVENTS

Admissions
Is your child starting school in September 2027?
If your child was born between 1st September 2022 and 31st August 2023, you will need to apply for a school place for September 2027. We would be delighted to welcome you to Folly Hill! Please contact the school office if you would like to book in for one of our upcoming open days.
We know that choosing a school for your child is a big decision – it can be both an exciting and nerve-wracking time for children and parents alike! We understand it can be a daunting process for parents, especially those who are going through this process for the first time - we are here to support families to ensure this important decision is the right one for each child’s learning journey.
We would encourage you to look at the different sections across our website as they contain a wealth of useful information about life at Folly Hill. You are, of course, also welcome to contact us with any specific enquiries you may have.
Getting Ready for School
Come & Visit!
We are so proud of our academy and warmly invite new families to visit us to experience first-hand the welcoming, inclusive and encouraging learning environment we offer. Mrs Freeman is available to lead small group tours on the following dates:
Tuesday 29 September at 9:00am, 10:00am or 11:00amTuesday 13 October at 9:00am, 10:00am or 11:00amTuesday 10 November at 9:00am, 10:00am or 11:00amTuesday 24 November at 9:00am, 10:00am or 11:00amTuesday 8 December at 9:00am, 10:00am or 11:00amTuesday 5 January at 9:00am, 10:00am or 11:00am
If you would like to book a tour, please contact the school office on 01252 716 121 or email info@follyhill.kite.academy with your preferred date(s) and time(s), and we will get back to you as soon as possible to confirm your place.
We look forward to welcoming you to Folly Hill Infant Academy.
How to Apply
You can apply for a school place for September 2027 between 2nd November 2026 and 15th January 2027.
If you live in Surrey, you can find further information about school admissions and apply online here or you can call 0300 200 1004. If you live in Hampshire, you can find further information about school admissions and apply online here or you can call 0300 555 1377.
Folly Hill has a Published Admissions Number (PAN) of 30. This means there are 30 places available in our Reception class.
The Kite Academy Trust is the admission authority for all its academies. The allocation of school places at initial entry (Reception Class) is managed by Surrey County Council's Admissions Team in accordance with our published admission arrangements (see below).
Once places have been offered by Surrey County Council's Admissions Team, any waiting list for places will be ranked according to our oversubscription criteria and managed by Folly Hill Infant Academy.

Moving Schools?
Applying for a place at a school during the academic year and outside of the normal round of admissions (as described above) is called an ‘in-year admission'. An in-year admission may be made, for example, if you move house and your child can no longer attend their current school. Any parent can apply for a place at Folly Hill at any time.
In-year admissions are co-ordinated by Surrey County Council's Admissions Team on our behalf. Further information can be found here. Applications should be made using the Surrey County Council in-year online portal here. Alternatively, please contact the Surrey County Council Admissions Team via schooladmissions@surreycc.gov.uk or 0300 200 1004 to request a paper form. Paper applications should be submitted to:
School Admissions TeamSurrey County CouncilPO Box 475ReigateRH2 2HP
Guidance notes can be found below.
Upon receipt of an in-year application, the Local Authority will process the application as quickly as possible, usually within 15 working days of receiving your fully completed application form. Where an application is refused, there is the right to appeal. Details of how to appeal can be found below.
Where an applicant is offered a school place following an in-year application, and the offer is accepted, arrangements will be made for the child to start school as soon as possible, particularly where the child is out of school.

Right to Appeal
All parents have a right to express a preference for the school they would like their child to attend. The admission authority must offer a place at that school unless there is a legal reason for refusing a place. All parents have the right to appeal against any decision made by or on behalf of an admission authority as to the school their child attends under legislation produced by the Department for Education (DfE). For information about the appeals process, please visit www.surreycc.gov.uk/schoolappeals

Our admissions arrangements for the academic year 2028/29 will be determined by the Board of Trustees at their meeting on 11th February 2027.

Governors
In accordance with the Kite Academy Trust's governance structure as defined in its Articles of Association, Folly Hill Infant Academy has a local advisory body, known as an Academy Council. The Academy Council is formed of Governors with a breadth of experience and skills who volunteer their time to ensure the very best outcomes for all children at the academy.
As a sub-committee of The Kite Academy Trust Board of Trustees, the role of the Academy Council is:
To ensure that the academy provides the highest possible level of education for all children;
To ensure the safety and welfare of children and staff;
To ensure the Trust’s vision and values are well-embedded and promoted by leaders amongst staff, children and stakeholders;
To ensure that support and robust challenge is given to the Academy Head;
To ensure that the leadership of the academy have high expectations for all children, including those with special needs;
To ensure the curriculum is ambitious with appropriate breadth for all children in the academy;
To ensure the Academy Improvement Plan delivers improvement;
To ensure risk is both managed and reported to the Trust Board;
To ensure that the academy has effective and appropriate systems and procedures in place;
To be accountable to stakeholders (Board of Trustees, parents, pupils, staff and local community)
An Academy Council is constituted as follows:
2 Local Community Governors (minimum)
The Academy Head is automatically a Governor by virtue of their position. Two Parent Governors are elected by parents of the academy and the Staff Governor is elected by employees of the academy. Local Community Governors are co-opted as necessary to provide the skills and experience needed by the Academy Council. In addition, the Academy Council may appoint other persons as Associate Academy Council Members to address any specifically identified skill gaps or to support any particular challenges that they may be facing. With the exception of the Academy Head, Governors serve a four year term and are eligible for re-appointment (subject to an election where necessary for Staff and Parent Governors). The positions of Chair and Vice-Chair are elected, and Governors with responsibility for Safeguarding and Special Educational Needs & Disability (SEND) nominated, by the Governors on an annual basis.
The Academy Council meets a minimum of four times during the academic year. The primary purpose of the meetings is to review and monitor the progress of the Academy Improvement Plan, identify any areas of risk to be reported to the Trust Board, and consider the medium and long-term strategic development of the academy. Monitoring mainly involves talking to children and staff, visiting classrooms to see learning in action, and examining children’s work books and other documentary material. Governors also take the opportunity to talk with families at Parents’ Evenings.
Across the Trust, Academy Council Governors work in collaboration with other Academy Councils to support the improvement, development and success of each academy in the Kite Academy Trust. Training opportunities for Governors are provided by the Kite Academy Trust.

pageCache.pageTitle: Sports Premium - Folly Hill Infant Academy
pageCache.text:
Sports Premium
What is the Sports Premium grant?
The Government has provided additional funding for primary schools since 2013 in order to improve the provision of physical education and sport. This funding comes from the Departments for Education, Health and Culture, Media and Sport.
The funding can only be spent on provision for PE and sport in schools. We are held accountable for how we have used the additional funding to support pupil progress and participation in PE and school sport. We are required to publish information about how we have used the additional funding, including details about our sports provision alongside curriculum details.
How much money do we receive?
All schools with 17 or more primary-aged pupils receive a lump sum of £8000 plus a premium of £5 per pupil.
How do we decide what to spend it on?
Our rationale for the use of Sports Premium funding, which has been agreed by the Governors, is that we must use it so that:
all children should benefit regardless of their sporting ability
staff have access to training opportunities and continued professional development
children have opportunities to compete in tournaments and events with other schools
we build up a partnership with other schools and clubs
some activities and clubs may be subsidised so that all pupils have opportunities, eg. extra-curricular clubs, swimming lessons
How do we evaluate our spending?
Over the course of the academic year we will evaluate the impact of the funding as part of our regular school evaluations and through pupil voice. We will look at how well we use the Sports Premium to improve the quality and breadth of PE and sporting provision, including increasing participation at all levels so that pupils develop healthy lifestyles and reach the performance levels they are capable of. We aim to increase the activity of all children in school, in particular reluctant children. We have already seen an increase in the numbers of pupils entering events and joining clubs.

Rocksteady
In-school rock and pop band lessons with Rocksteady
We partner with Rocksteady Music School to deliver fun and inclusive rock and pop band lessons, right here at Folly Hill Infant Academy! These weekly music lessons take place in school and are led by highly trained professional musicians who know how to inspire a love for music.
It’s the perfect way for children to learn new musical skills, make friends and have fun, all whilst boosting confidence, wellbeing, social skills and academic achievement.
More about Rocksteady:
• There’s no experience necessary and all instruments for lessons are provided.
• Lessons are open for children in Reception, Year 1 and Year 2.
• Children learn up to 300 instrument, band, and performance skills, whilst playing songs they love.
• Children can achieve an Ofqual-regulated Music qualification, accredited by Trinity College London, without having to take a single exam.
• End of term concerts so you can see just how far they have come.
• Parents receive regular updates about their child’s progress, including photos and videos.
If your child would like to experience the magic of learning music, you can sign up to Rocksteady at: rocksteadymusicschool.com/parents
Tel: 0330 113 0330 (Mon–Thurs 8am-8pm, Fri 8am-6pm, calls charged at local rate)

School Lunch
From 1st September 2026, Dolce has been appointed as the new catering provider for all schools in The Kite Academy Trust.
Dolce Catering forms part of the Impact Food Group (IFG), a highly regarded and award-winning UK education caterer.
From 1st September, Dolce will use the School Grid app for all menu choices and meal bookings. This is a one stop place where you can view all menu choices, pre-order meals daily, weekly or termly. Importantly, it also provides you with the opportunity to record any allergies or special dietary requirements your child may have, sharing these directly with Dolce.
Over the summer holidays, parents will receive an email directly from School Grid in order to register and set up your account. Please can we ask that you register and complete all related tasks, including ordering meals for the first few days of term, in readiness for school to reopen on Thursday 3rd September. This will support a smooth transition to the new academic year.
Please note that ALL children in Reception, Year 1 and Year 2 will continue to receive a government-funded Universal Infant Free School Meal so there is no charge for school meals here at Folly Hill.

Uniform
In support of the ‘Reduce, Reuse, Recycle’ environmental program, we are encouraging the purchase of second hand uniform. This can be bought at one of the 'Friends Of Folly Hill' second hand uniform sales or ordered by emailing them at friends@follyhill.kite.academy.
New school uniform, book bags and PE bags can be ordered from Brenda's, either on-line or from their Camberley store - full details here or from their website www.brendas.co.uk.
Children are expected to wear school uniform at all times in school. Please ensure that all items of clothing are labelled clearly.
Our uniform consists of:
pale blue polo shirt with academy logo or plain pale blue polo shirt
royal blue sweat shirt or cardigan with academy logo
grey trousers/knee length shorts/ knee length pinafore dress/ knee length skirt
blue gingham dress in summer
white/grey/black socks or grey/black tights
black sturdy shoes (no trainers please)
royal blue PE t-shirt with academy logo or plan royal blue t-shirt
plain white PE shorts
black jogging bottoms
black PE plimsolls or trainers
For safety reasons, no jewellery (earrings included except studs) is permitted. The school cannot be responsible for the safety of watches. Alert bracelets can be worn.
Suitable footwear for school during the summer months.
Please could children not wear open toe sandals or flip flops. The children spend a lot of time outdoors playing, pond dipping, running around the playground etc and we have found that they do trip over more frequently in inappropriate shoes.
